page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-128 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. The server provides 16 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.6 GHz with a single thread per core, offering 16 unshared vCPUs free from simultaneous multithreading overhead. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

Hardware provisioning does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network block storage for root filesystems and persistent application data. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because each vCPU is backed by a dedicated execution engine, the configuration avoids core-sharing contention and maintains consistent multi-threaded throughput on 64-bit Arm (aarch64) runtime environments.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides favorable resource density for memory-bound workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets. Primary architectural tradeoffs involve dependence on network storage and necessary verification of Arm binary compatibility. VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-128 is designed for in-memory key-value databases, analytics caching nodes, ETL pipelines, and general memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-128 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on 64-bit Arm architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores from an Ampere AmpereOne-M processor clocked at 3.6 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs with single-threaded core isolation. The system contains 128.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive operations. Hardware resources do not feature integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage must be attached over the network, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated core topology eliminates execution interference from noisy neighbors, offering consistent computation. The configuration provides strong memory density without the cost profile of legacy architectures, making it well matched for in-memory databases, Redis caches, batch data processing, and distributed microservices.
